description: Install asciiam, create a sized target, select a renderer, and start the animation lifecycle.
text:
asciiam renders an animated glyph grid into a canvas owned by an HTML element or into a canvas supplied by the caller. Prerequisites A browser with requestAnimationFrame and Canvas 2D. WebGL2 when using the default GPU-first renderer; Canvas 2D is used when WebGL2 is unavailable. A target element with non-zero width and height. Install from npm terminal npm install @staticcanvas/asciiam app.js import asciiam from '@staticcanvas/asciiam'; const animation = new asciiam('#hero', { ...asciiam.presets.heroWave, renderer: 'auto' }); animation.start(); The package export resolves to dist/asciiam.mjs in ESM-aware runtimes. A direct browser import can use the same module artifact without a bundler: index.html
Load a browser bundle index.html

Content remains above the ASCII media surface.

Choose a renderer Value Selection behavior Fallback auto Attempts WebGL2 first. Canvas 2D webgl2 Explicitly requests WebGL2. Canvas 2D canvas2d Uses Canvas 2D. None Inspect the resolved backend after construction: app.js const info = animation.getRendererInfo(); console.log(info.requested, info.backend); animation.setRenderer('canvas2d'); Lifecycle Call start() after construction. Call stop() to retain the instance and its state without scheduling frames. Call destroy() when the target is no longer used. stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Constructed Constructed --> Running: start() Running --> Stopped: stop() / off-screen / hidden tab Stopped --> Running: start() / visible Running --> Destroyed: destroy() Stopped --> Destroyed: destroy() Destroyed --> [*] Next steps Review renderers and performance. Build animation sequences. Edit configurations in Usage examples. Preview configurations in the preset gallery. Consult the API reference. API reference API Type Default Purpose new asciiam(target, options) constructor — Creates one renderer and animation state container. renderer option auto Selects automatic, WebGL2, or Canvas 2D rendering. dist/asciiam.mjs ESM artifact — Supports package resolution and direct browser module imports. dist/asciiam.cjs CommonJS artifact — Supports require('@staticcanvas/asciiam'). start() method — Starts or resumes frame scheduling. stop() method — Stops frame scheduling without removing the canvas. destroy() method — Removes observers, listeners, renderer resources, and the owned canvas.
title: Getting started

description: Select WebGL2 or Canvas 2D and control quality, frame rate, memory, and multi-instance behavior.
text:
asciiam separates animation-state calculation from presentation. WebGL2 uploads one glyph instance buffer and draws the visible glyphs as instanced quads. Canvas 2D uses cached glyph atlases and mode-specific shortcuts where possible.
Renderer selection app.js
const animation = new asciiam('#target', { renderer: 'auto', powerPreference: 'high-performance', quality: 'ultra' }); auto is appropriate for most integrations. Use canvas2d for deterministic CPU rendering or environments that limit WebGL contexts. Use webgl2 when the requested renderer must be recorded as GPU-first while retaining fallback behavior.
WebGL2 fallback flow flowchart TD A[Construct instance] --> B{renderer} B -->|canvas2d| C[Canvas 2D] B -->|auto or webgl2| D{WebGL2 context and shaders available?} D -->|yes| E[Instanced WebGL2 renderer] D -->|no| C E --> F{Context lost?} F -->|yes| C F -->|no| E The rendererFallback event reports context-loss fallback. rendererChange reports a requested or resolved backend change.
Quality tiers Tier Maximum DPR Density Font levels Alpha levels Canvas atlas Static wave cache high 3 0.9 6 64 No No balanced 2 1.0 5 32 No No performance 1.5 1.4 4 16 Yes No ultra 1 2.4 2 8 Yes Yes Higher density values produce fewer cells because they increase cell spacing. targetFPS: null does not impose a library frame cap; the browser display and scheduler remain the physical limit.
Multiple instances All running instances share one requestAnimationFrame scheduler. Each instance retains independent timing, visibility, renderer, and target state. For galleries or grids, construct only visible previews and destroy off-screen instances after a short delay. Browsers limit the number of simultaneous WebGL contexts.
3D rendering boundary The mesh mode projects bounded geometry into cell-resolution depth and luminance buffers, then uses the existing WebGL2 or Canvas 2D glyph presentation path. It does not turn the WebGL2 backend into a general scene renderer. See 3D meshes and models for geometry contracts, glTF/GLB input, controls, and limits.
Poly Haven models are recorded as a CC0 candidate source for optional demonstrations. Khronos glTF Sample Assets are recorded for format fixtures, with per-model license verification required. The glTF 2.0 specification is the format reference for core .gltf and .glb input. Base-format parsing is dependency-free; codecs for compressed extensions are not bundled, loaded, or injectable. Files requiring those extensions will fail with a format diagnostic.
API reference Property or method Type Default Effect renderer auto | webgl2 | canvas2d auto Selects the presentation backend. powerPreference high-performance | low-power | default high-performance Passes an adapter preference to WebGL2. quality quality name balanced Applies tier values. maxDPR number tier value Caps backing-store pixel ratio. targetFPS number or null null Adds a per-instance frame cap when numeric. setRenderer(value) method — Replaces the presentation canvas while retaining instance state. getRendererInfo() method — Returns requested and resolved renderer information. mesh mode built in — Projects points, wireframes, or solid triangles into ASCII cells. setModel(source) async method — Loads core glTF 2.0 or GLB v2; required compression extensions are rejected.
title: Renderers and performance

description: Own targets, renderer instances, application teardown, accessibility, and custom-mode boundaries.
text:
One asciiam instance owns one presentation surface and its lifecycle state. Applications own the target element, configuration, and the point at which the instance is destroyed.
Target ownership Pass a selector, an element, or an existing canvas. A container target receives an owned canvas as its first child; an existing canvas remains application-owned. The target must have a measurable width and height before construction.
app.js
const target = document.querySelector('#hero-media'); const animation = new asciiam(target, { renderer: 'auto' }); animation.start(); setTarget() moves an owned presentation canvas between container elements without creating a second scheduler entry or replacing event subscriptions. Use a new instance when two surfaces must render concurrently.
Pointer movement and pointer/touch presses are observed on the target container. The canvas remains pointer-transparent, so application controls and links keep their normal event targets. Use hoverZone for a moving local field and clickZone for a triggered pulse.
Application teardown Call stop() when an instance may resume. Call destroy() when its view or target is removed. Destruction removes scheduler membership, observers, event listeners, renderer resources, decoded image-frame data, and the canvas when asciiam created it.
view.js
const animation = new asciiam('#preview', asciiam.presets.heroWave); animation.start(); export function disposePreview() { animation.destroy(); } Keep the unsubscribe function returned by on() when a listener has a shorter lifetime than the instance.
Visibility and reduced motion Running instances share one requestAnimationFrame scheduler. Intersection and document-visibility observers prevent off-screen or hidden instances from advancing. When prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matches and respectReducedMotion is enabled, the instance renders a static frame instead of scheduling animation.
The canvas is decorative by default and is created with aria-hidden="true" and role="presentation". Put an accessible name or equivalent text on the surrounding content when the ASCII result communicates information rather than decoration.
Custom-mode boundary Use asciiam.registerMode() for a named mode shared by instances. Use customCell with mode: 'custom' for instance-local behavior. A callback runs once per dense grid cell per frame, so avoid allocation, DOM access, network access, and repeated color parsing inside it.
modes.js
asciiam.registerMode('diagonalBands', (cell) => { const phase = (cell.col + cell.row) * 0.25 - cell.time * 2; const intensity = (Math.sin(phase) + 1) / 2; return cell.set('#', intensity, intensity, intensity > 0.8); }); Registered names are process-global. Choose names that will not collide with built-in or third-party modes.
Integration flow flowchart TD A[Application creates sized target] --> B[Construct asciiam instance] B --> C[Bind events or load image] C --> D[start] D --> E{View remains mounted?} E -->|yes| F[stop and start as needed] F --> E E -->|no| G[destroy] API reference API Owner Result new asciiam(target, options?) application Creates one instance and resolves a presentation backend. start() instance Starts or resumes scheduler participation. stop() instance Stops scheduling while retaining state and resources. destroy() instance Releases instance-owned resources and listeners. setTarget(target) application Moves the presentation surface to another container. on(event, listener) application Subscribes and returns an unsubscribe function. registerMode(name, callback) process Registers a named dense-cell callback. respectReducedMotion option Defaults to true; renders a static frame for reduced motion.
title: Integration and lifecycle

description: Configure dense fields, spatial effects, reveals, sparse particles, images, and custom cells.
text:
Modes determine how each frame selects glyph, intensity, opacity, weight, and optional color.
Built-in modes Mode Processing model Primary controls wave dense field direction, ambient, bandWidth current dense field speed, opacity bounds ripple cached spatial field align, speed vortex cached spatial field align, speed plasma cached spatial field speed, gradient fadeIn, fadeOut timed reveal revealDirection, loop irisIn, irisOut radial transition reveal align, loop dissolveIn, dissolveOut seeded directional dissolve revealDirection, loop lumaFold coined folded-luminance ridges speed, opacity bounds riftLace coined intersecting seam lattice speed, character set echoBloom coined concentric echo blossoms align, speed glitch dense displacement glitchIntensity typewriter timed reveal typewriterDuration matrix, snow, sparkle sparse particles matching density option fire, starfield, orbit sparse particles matching density option hoverZone pointer-local dense field interactionRadius, setCursor() clickZone triggered expanding dense field interactionRadius, interactionDuration, triggerInteraction() image sampled image grid image and mask options custom callback customCell Change mode app.js
animation.setMode('vortex'); animation.setOption('align', 'top-left'); animation.setOption('speed', 0.65); Manual setMode() interrupts an active sequence and emits sequenceInterrupt. Sequence step changes use the internal mode transition without treating the change as manual input.
Mode selection changes only the animation algorithm. A loaded image remains the glyph source, including for irisIn, irisOut, dissolveIn, dissolveOut, lumaFold, riftLace, and echoBloom. Preset selection retains the active global mode.
revealDirection supports left-to-right, right-to-left, top-to-bottom, bottom-to-top, diagonal, center, and edges. Changing the direction restarts the local reveal timeline so the result is visible immediately.
Custom mode app.js
asciiam.registerMode('diagonalBands', (api) => { const phase = (api.col + api.row) * 0.25 - api.time * 2; const intensity = (Math.sin(phase) + 1) / 2; return api.set('#', intensity, intensity, intensity > 0.8); }); animation.setMode('diagonalBands'); Pointer interaction modes hoverZone follows pointer movement over the target. setCursor(x, y) supplies the same coordinates programmatically and setCursor(null) clears them. Without an active pointer coordinate, the mode retains only its low-opacity seeded field.
clickZone starts an expanding pulse on pointer or touch press. Call triggerInteraction(x, y) to start it from application coordinates. Calling triggerInteraction() without coordinates uses the current align origin.
app.js
animation.setMode('clickZone'); animation.setOption('interactionRadius', 240); animation.setOption('interactionDuration', 1.4); animation.triggerInteraction(); Alignment support align accepts nine anchors: top-left, top, top-right, left, center, right, bottom-left, bottom, and bottom-right.
Mode or feature Alignment effect current Offsets cached field phases. ripple, vortex, plasma, echoBloom Sets the spatial origin. irisIn, irisOut Sets the reveal centre. starfield, orbit Sets the particle projection or orbit origin. Legacy image radial ripple Sets its cached radial origin. clickZone programmatic trigger Supplies the origin when triggerInteraction() receives no coordinates. Alignment does not affect directional, coordinate-global, or pointer-defined modes where a fixed origin has no meaningful role.
API reference API Type Default Effect mode mode name wave Selects the active animation algorithm. speed number 1 Scales the instance timeline. setMode(mode) method — Changes mode and restarts its local timeline. registerMode(name, fn) static method — Registers a named cell callback. customCell(api) function null Supplies cells when mode is custom. interactionRadius CSS pixels 180 Sets hover extent and click-pulse travel distance. interactionDuration seconds 1.1 Sets click-pulse duration. triggerInteraction(x?, y?) method aligned origin Starts a click-zone pulse. Image-backed modes loaded image grid none Applies the selected global mode to sampled glyphs.
title: Animation modes

description: Operational guidance for integration, rendering, animations, character sets, sequences, images, and the web utility.
text: Guides explain how application integration and the web utility map to runtime configuration, and when an option changes renderer state, cached data, image samples, or sequence behavior.
title: Guides

description: Select the default glyph inventory, density ramps, symbolic palettes, or a custom ordered string.
text:
Character sets map a normalized mode intensity or sampled image luminance to a glyph index. The first character represents the lowest value and the last character represents the highest value.
Default character set The default charSet and imageChars value is asciiam.CHARACTER_SETS.asciiExtended. It contains 190 characters in this order:
The 95 printable ASCII code points from U+0020 SPACE through U+007E TILDE. The 95 Latin-1 code points from U+00A1 INVERTED EXCLAMATION MARK through U+00FF LATIN SMALL LETTER Y WITH DIAERESIS. The default favors glyph variety and broad Latin coverage. It is ordered by code point, not measured visual density. Use density, extended, technical, or another intentionally ordered ramp when predictable light-to-dark image conversion is more important than variation.
app.js
const animation = new asciiam('#hero', { charSet: asciiam.CHARACTER_SETS.asciiExtended, imageChars: asciiam.CHARACTER_SETS.density }); charSet controls procedural modes. imageChars controls image luminance mapping and may be configured independently.
Included sets Name Value or composition Intended use density .:-=+*#%@ Compact, predictable luminance ramp. ascii U+0020–U+007E Printable ASCII variety. asciiExtended printable ASCII plus U+00A1–U+00FF Default broad Latin inventory. extended hand-ordered 70-character photographic ramp Image conversion with more density steps. alphanumeric space, digits, upper- and lowercase Latin letters Text-oriented fields without punctuation. uppercase space and A–Z Uppercase terminal fields. lowercase space and a–z Lowercase text fields. symbols space and printable ASCII punctuation Symbol-only fields. boxDrawing lines, corners, joins, shades, and blocks Diagram and terminal-grid textures. arrows cardinal, diagonal, and double arrows Directional fields. math operators and set/calculus symbols Mathematical textures. blocks space and ░▒▓█ Five-level block shading. minimal .oO@ Small portable five-level ramp. technical .·:+=*#%@ Ten-level technical display ramp. geometric space plus circular, square, triangular, and diamond forms Shape transitions and interaction zones. circuit ·-+=oO0#@ Circuit and node-like textures. waves ~≈≋∿ Low-cardinality flowing fields. terminal space, binary digits, brackets, operators, and density marks Terminal and protocol-like textures. binary 01 Binary rain and masks. binaryWide weighted 0 and 1 repetition Binary output with biased selection. braille ordered Braille fill forms Compact dot-density fields. japanese space, binary digits, and selected Katakana Matrix-style fields. punctuation hand-ordered punctuation and letters Photographic ASCII convention. Availability depends on the selected font. Missing glyphs may render as replacement boxes. Choose a font that covers non-ASCII sets and test it on target platforms.
Custom ordered sets Any JavaScript string is accepted. Include a leading space when zero intensity should produce no visible glyph. Use at least two distinct characters so intensity can select more than one result.
app.js
animation.setOption('charSet', ' .·oO0@'); animation.setOption('imageChars', ' .:-=+*#%@'); Repeated characters are allowed and weight selection toward those glyphs. binaryWide, for example, intentionally repeats digits.
API reference API Type Default Effect asciiam.CHARACTER_SETS record of strings included sets Provides named character inventories and ramps. charSet string asciiExtended Maps procedural intensity to glyphs. imageChars string asciiExtended Maps sampled image luminance to glyphs. setOption('charSet', value) method — Rebuilds dependent glyph atlases and static-wave caches. setOption('imageChars', value) method — Resamples loaded image sources and rebuilds dependent atlases.
title: Character sets

description: Edit and run configurations from the minimum constructor through interaction, image, sequence, and complete serializable examples.
text:
The playground runs one version-aligned local renderer instance and replaces it only after the editor contains valid JSON. It does not depend on npm or a CDN, so a source checkout remains usable before a package release reaches a registry.
Editing model Select an example, edit its option object, and use Run or pause briefly for the debounced preview update. Reset restores the selected example. View in web utility transfers the current JSON-safe configuration through the URL; the web utility then exposes its complete control surface.
The editor accepts JSON because it can be validated without evaluating arbitrary JavaScript. Callbacks such as onReady, sequence callbacks, and customCell are functions and therefore belong in application source rather than the serializable editor.
Package usage app.js
import asciiam from '@staticcanvas/asciiam'; const options = { mode: 'wave', color: '#72F1B8' }; const animation = new asciiam('#preview', options); animation.start(); Registry installation may lag the repository until a release is published. The live playground always imports the documentation build’s bundled ESM file.
API reference Playground surface Input Behavior Example selector Included example Replaces editor text and renderer state. Configuration editor JSON object Debounces parsing and creates one replacement renderer after valid input. Run Valid JSON object Applies the current configuration immediately. Reset Selected example Restores the authored option object. Copy Current editor text Copies the configuration JSON. View in web utility Valid JSON-safe options Encodes configuration into the utility URL without registry access.
title: Usage examples

description: Run ordered, image-aware animation nodes with controlled timing, transitions, callbacks, and looping.
text:
A sequence controls one renderer. Each node selects a mode, duration, optional delay, image-source action, mode-repeat policy, option overrides, and lifecycle callbacks. The web utility displays nodes left to right in playback order; its image selector can retain the current source, clear it, or load one of the included images.
repeat and sequence loop control different boundaries. A step with repeat: true restarts a finite mode such as fadeIn, fadeOut, irisIn, dissolveOut, or typewriter while that step remains active. It defaults to false, so a finite mode reaches its final frame and holds it until the next step. Sequence loop controls whether playback returns to the first step after the final step.
An incoming step can also declare a morph transition. asciiam captures the outgoing frame once, starts the incoming mode, and fades the captured frame over it. Only the incoming algorithm remains live, so the transition does not run two animation modes concurrently. The default transition is cut; reduced-motion preference also resolves morphs to cuts.
Configure the requested flow The following sequence runs ripple for five seconds, fades out, fades in, and repeats.
app.js
animation.setSequence([ { mode: 'ripple', duration: 5 }, { mode: 'fadeOut', duration: 5, repeat: false, transition: { type: 'morph', duration: 0.8, easing: 'easeInOut' } }, { mode: 'fadeIn', duration: 1, transition: { type: 'morph', duration: 0.8, easing: 'easeInOut' } } ], { loop: true, autoplay: true, onStepStart(detail) { console.log(detail.index, detail.step.mode); } }); Move between images Set image to a URL to decode and sample a new source before that node starts. Omit the field to retain the current source, or use null to clear image data and return to a procedural grid. A node’s delay elapses first; its duration does not begin until the new image is ready. This prevents decode time from shortening the visible node.
animation.setSequence([ { mode: 'fadeIn', image: '/media/product-front.webp', duration: 3 }, { mode: 'lumaFold', image: '/media/product-detail.webp', imageOptions: { animated: false }, duration: 4, transition: { type: 'morph', duration: 0.6, easing: 'easeInOut' } }, { mode: 'wave', image: null, duration: 2 } ], { autoplay: true, loop: true }); animation.on('sequenceStepError', ({ index, error }) => { console.error(`Image for node ${index + 1} could not be loaded`, error); }); An image failure pauses the sequence, calls the node’s optional onError, and emits sequenceStepError. Correct the source or seek to another node before resuming.
delay staggers the start of a step. During the delay, the prior frame state continues. duration begins after the delay completes.
Sequence state stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Configured: setSequence() Configured --> Waiting: playSequence() + delay Configured --> Playing: playSequence() Waiting --> Loading: node declares a new image Loading --> Playing: image decoded and sampled Loading --> Paused: image error Waiting --> Playing: delay elapsed, image retained or cleared Playing --> Waiting: next step has delay Playing --> Playing: next step Playing --> Paused: pauseSequence() Paused --> Playing: playSequence() Playing --> Complete: last step and loop=false Playing --> Configured: stopSequence() Playing --> Interrupted: manual setMode() Callbacks and events Step callbacks receive (detail, animation). The same lifecycle is available through on() event subscriptions when configuration should remain serializable.
API reference API Input Result setSequence(steps, options) step array, sequence options Configures a sequence and returns the instance. playSequence(index?) optional start index Starts or resumes playback. pauseSequence(reason?) optional reason Pauses at the current step. stopSequence() none Stops playback and resets sequence position. clearSequence() none Removes sequence configuration. seekSequence(index) numeric index Interrupts the current step and selects another. nextSequenceStep() none Advances one step using loop policy. getSequenceState() none Returns configured, running, completed, index, length, loop, elapsed, waiting, loading, and morph state. step.image string, null, or omitted Loads a source, clears the current source, or retains it. step.imageOptions object Passes image decode hints such as animated to setImage(). step.onError callback Runs when the node’s image cannot be decoded. step.repeat boolean, default false Repeats a finite mode timeline while the step remains active. step.transition { type, duration, easing } Selects an incoming cut or snapshot morph; duration uses seconds. options.loop boolean Legacy per-mode repeat input; step.repeat is the explicit sequence form. sequenceMorphStart event Emitted after the outgoing frame is captured. sequenceMorphComplete event Emitted after the outgoing snapshot reaches zero opacity. sequenceStepError event Emitted when a node image fails; playback pauses.
title: Animation sequences

description: Preview included presets, copy their option objects, or open them in the web utility.
text:
The gallery constructs previews only near the viewport and keeps no more than six renderer instances active. Off-screen instances are destroyed after a short delay. This avoids exhausting browser WebGL context limits while retaining live previews.
imageReveal requires an image source and therefore displays a non-rendering placeholder until configured in the web utility. Place documentation gallery source images in docs/assets/images and add explicit metadata before using them in content.
API reference Gallery action Output Copy configuration JavaScript declaration containing the preset options. Open in utility Opens the app with ?preset=<name>. Search Filters by preset name or mode. Category filter Filters field, spatial, particle, reveal, or image presets.
title: Preset gallery

description: Constructor, static members, options, methods, events, renderer data, sequence objects, and callback contracts.
text:
The package exports the asciiam class as its default export and provides TypeScript declarations in src/asciiam.d.ts.
Choose an integration path Goal Start with Then use Render one animation new asciiam(target, options) setOption(), setMode() Prefer GPU with a safe fallback renderer: 'auto' getRendererInfo(), rendererFallback Play an ordered animation story setSequence(steps, options) sequence events and callbacks Turn an image into animated ASCII setImage(source) image mask and RGB range options Render geometry or a model meshPrimitive, setMesh(), or setModel() mesh controls and model events Own application cleanup instance lifecycle stop() or destroy() All durations are expressed in seconds, dimensions and font sizes use CSS pixels unless noted, and normalized coordinates use the inclusive 0–1 range. Mutating methods apply to the live instance; sequence methods return the instance for chaining.
Constructor app.js
import asciiam from '@staticcanvas/asciiam'; const animation = new asciiam('#target', { mode: 'wave', renderer: 'auto', quality: 'balanced' }); new asciiam(target, options?) Parameter Type Required Description target CSS selector, HTMLElement, or HTMLCanvasElement Yes Container that receives an owned canvas, or a caller-owned canvas. options asciiamOptions No Initial renderer, mode, presentation, image, and lifecycle configuration. The constructor throws when the target cannot be found or when renderer has an unsupported value. If neither Canvas 2D nor WebGL2 can initialize, the instance becomes a no-op and logs a warning.
Target ownership Passing a container lets asciiam create and own its presentation canvas. Passing an HTMLCanvasElement uses the caller-supplied canvas. In both cases, call destroy() before permanently removing the instance so renderer resources and observers are released.
Static members Member Type Description asciiam.BUILT_IN_MODES readonly mode-name array Canonical inventory implemented by the library. asciiam.QUALITY record Quality-tier values for DPR, density, font levels, alpha levels, and caches. asciiam.CHARACTER_SETS record Named glyph strings ordered for density mapping. asciiam.presets record Included option objects keyed by preset name. asciiam.isSupported() method Returns whether WebGL2 or Canvas 2D context creation succeeds. asciiam.registerMode(name, fn) method Registers a named custom cell callback. asciiam.createMeshPrimitive(name, options?) method Creates a cube, plane, icosphere, or torus MeshData. asciiam.loadModel(source, options?) async method Decodes glTF 2.0 or GLB v2 without constructing a renderer. Core options Property Type Default Description mode mode string wave Selects the active animation algorithm. quality high | balanced | performance | ultra balanced Applies one quality tier. renderer auto | webgl2 | canvas2d auto when GPU preference is enabled Selects GPU-first, explicit WebGL2, or Canvas 2D presentation. charSet string asciiExtended Supplies glyphs used by procedural modes. fontFamily string IBM Plex Mono fallback stack Sets glyph measurement and rasterization fonts. fontSize number 14 Sets the base font size in CSS pixels. density number quality-tier value Scales glyph-cell spacing. color CSS color string #4FA8FF Sets the fallback glyph color. background CSS color string transparent Sets the renderer clear color. speed number 1 Scales the animation timeline. direction horizontal | vertical | diagonal horizontal Sets wave travel direction. revealDirection reveal direction string center Sets horizontal, vertical, diagonal, center-out, or edge-in reveal order. align nine-position spatial alignment center Sets the origin for compatible spatial modes. minOpacity number 0.05 Sets the lower procedural opacity bound. maxOpacity number 0.85 Sets the upper procedural opacity bound. boldOnPeak boolean true Uses bold font variants for high-intensity cells. loop boolean true Loops mode-local reveal timelines. edgeFade number 0 Applies cached edge attenuation. Mesh and model options Property Type Default Description meshPrimitive cube | plane | icosphere | torus | null null Creates dependency-free geometry during construction. meshStyle points | wireframe | solid wireframe Selects cell rasterization. meshProjection perspective | orthographic perspective Selects projection. meshCamera camera object or null null Overrides position, target, up, FOV, clipping, and orthographic scale. meshTransform transform object or null null Sets position, Euler rotation, and scale. meshLight light object or null null Sets directional-light direction, ambient, and intensity. meshAutoRotate boolean true Applies elapsed-time rotation. meshRotationSpeed three-number array [0.2, 0.45, 0.1] Sets radians per second on X, Y, and Z. meshMaxVertices positive integer 100000 Rejects larger normalized geometry. meshMaxPrimitives positive integer 100000 Rejects larger normalized geometry. setMesh(mesh), clearMesh(), and getMeshInfo() manage typed-array geometry. setModel(source, options?) and clearModel() manage abortable glTF/GLB loading. Model sources may be URLs, blobs, byte buffers, or parsed glTF objects. See 3D meshes and models for supported format features and explicit exclusions.
Renderer and performance options Property Type Default Description powerPreference high-performance | low-power | default high-performance Passes a preference to WebGL2 context creation. preferGPU boolean true Makes an omitted renderer GPU-first; false defaults to Canvas 2D. desynchronized boolean true when GPU preference is enabled Requests a low-latency presentation context. maxDPR number quality-tier value Caps backing-store device pixel ratio. targetFPS number or null quality-tier value (null) Adds a frame interval when numeric. fontLevels number quality-tier value Sets quantized font-size variants. alphaLevels number quality-tier value Sets opacity quantization. useGlyphAtlas boolean quality-tier value Enables the Canvas 2D solid glyph atlas. cacheStaticWave boolean quality-tier value Enables Ultra’s static horizontal wave cache when compatible. showStats boolean false Enables attached stats output. respectReducedMotion boolean true Draws a static frame when reduced motion is requested. Color and backdrop options Property Type Default Description gradient gradient object or null null Applies linear, radial, or cubic multi-stop glyph color. backdrop backdrop object or null null Draws a solid or gradient surface in the selected layer. trail number 0 Sets retained-frame overlay opacity. trailColor CSS color #070809 Sets the retained-frame overlay color. pulse { amplitude, speed } or null null Applies a frame-level opacity multiplier. colorAnimation color animation object or null null Applies hueRotate or breathe. cursor cursor options or null null Raises opacity near pointer or supplied coordinates. interactionRadius CSS pixels 180 Sets hover-zone extent and click-zone travel distance. interactionDuration seconds 1.1 Sets click-zone pulse duration. Gradient object Property Type Default Description type linear | radial | cubic linear behavior Selects gradient geometry or interpolation. stops CSS colors or { offset, color }[] blue and purple defaults Sets colors and optional explicit offsets. steps integer from 1 through 6 2 Expands simple color arrays into output stops. angle number 0 Sets linear gradient degrees. center [x, y] [0.5, 0.5] Sets radial center as normalized coordinates. radius number 0.75 Sets radial radius relative to the largest dimension. animate boolean false Rotates the angle over time. Backdrop object Property Type Default Description enabled boolean false Enables the backdrop. opacity number 0.5 Sets backdrop alpha. color CSS color #0a0c10 Sets solid or fallback color. placement behind | over behind Draws before glyphs or composites after them. over at opacity 1 covers the animation. gradient gradient object or null null Sets backdrop gradient color. Image options Property Type Default Description image URL string or null null Loads an initial image. imageChars string asciiExtended Maps sampled brightness to glyphs. fit cover | contain cover Crops or letterboxes the sampled source. imageScale number 1 Applies centered source zoom. imageScaleX number 1 Scales sampled output width around its centre. imageScaleY number 1 Scales sampled output height around its centre. imageFov number 1 Controls visible source fraction. imageLuminance auto | normal | invert auto Controls silhouette-aware brightness mapping. colorFromImage boolean false Uses sampled RGB values for glyphs. animateImageMask boolean true Enables image mask animation. imageMaskMode legacy image mask string waveSweep Deprecated compatibility option for mode: 'image'; use global mode for new integrations. imageAnimationRange { min, max } or null null Restricts animation to an inclusive RGB box. animateImageFrames boolean true Plays captured or fallback-sampled GIF frames. imageFrameRate number 12 Caps fallback GIF sampling from 1 through 60 fps. Mode-specific options Property Type Default Mode ambient number 0.35 wave bandWidth number 0.14 wave snowDensity number 0.02 snow sparkleDensity number 0.05 sparkle fireDensity number 0.035 fire starfieldDensity number 0.018 starfield orbitDensity number 0.014 orbit glitchIntensity number 0.32 glitch typewriterDuration seconds 4.5 typewriter customCell function or null null custom Lifecycle and configuration methods Method Return Description start() void Starts or resumes scheduling. stop() void Stops scheduling and retains state. destroy() void Releases renderer, canvas, observers, event listeners, and scheduler membership. setMode(mode) void Selects a mode, resets local time, and interrupts manual sequence playback. setOption(key, value) void Updates an option and rebuilds affected caches or state. setTarget(target) void Moves the presentation canvas and target bindings. setImage(source, options?) Promise<HTMLImageElement | null> Decodes an image; supported browsers capture every GIF frame and its delay. clearImage() instance Cancels pending image work and clears sampled image state without changing the active mode. setMesh(mesh) instance Validates and retains typed-array point, line, or triangle geometry. clearMesh() instance Releases retained geometry and raster buffers. getMeshInfo() mesh summary Reports loaded topology and current raster controls. setModel(source, options?) Promise<MeshData | null> Loads abortable glTF 2.0 or GLB v2 input and retains its normalized mesh. clearModel() instance Cancels model loading and releases model geometry. setCursor(x, y?) void Sets cursor coordinates or clears them when x is null. triggerInteraction(x?, y?) void Starts a click-zone pulse; omitted coordinates use the aligned origin. attachStats(element) void Selects the element that receives FPS and grid output. Live configuration Use setOption() for focused changes and setMode() when the animation algorithm changes. Renderer changes should go through setRenderer() so backend resources are replaced consistently. Calling setMode() while a manual sequence is running interrupts that sequence and emits the corresponding interruption events.
Renderer methods setRenderer(renderer) Returns the resolved backend: webgl2 or canvas2d. The method replaces the presentation canvas when backend type changes and retains animation and sequence state.
getRendererInfo() Field Type Description requested auto | webgl2 | canvas2d Developer-selected policy. backend webgl2 | canvas2d Active presentation backend. gpuPreferred boolean Whether GPU preference is enabled. acceleration status string Reports GPU API preference, browser-managed Canvas, or no request. desynchronized boolean Resolved or requested low-latency context flag. willReadFrequently boolean Readback hint for the presentation context. Sequence objects Sequence step Property Type Required Description id string No Stable application identifier. label string No Application-facing label. mode mode string Yes Mode activated for the step. duration seconds No Active step duration. delay seconds No Wait before step activation. repeat boolean No Repeats a finite mode timeline within the step; defaults to false. image string, null, or omitted No Decodes a new source before timing starts, clears the source, or retains it when omitted. imageOptions image option record No Passes decode hints such as animated to setImage(). options option record No Step-local option overrides. transition transition object No Incoming cut or snapshot morph transition. onStart callback No Runs when the step starts. onComplete callback No Runs on normal completion. onInterrupt callback No Runs when interrupted. onError callback No Runs when the step image fails to load; playback pauses. Sequence options Property Type Default Description loop boolean true behavior Restarts after the final step. autoplay boolean false Starts after configuration. onStepStart callback null Runs for each start. onStepComplete callback null Runs for each normal completion. onStepInterrupt callback null Runs for each interruption. onComplete callback null Runs when a non-looping sequence completes. Sequence methods Method Return Description setSequence(steps, options?) instance Configures ordered steps. playSequence(startIndex?) instance Starts or resumes playback. pauseSequence(reason?) instance Pauses playback. stopSequence() instance Stops and resets playback. clearSequence() instance Removes sequence configuration. seekSequence(index) instance Interrupts and selects a normalized index. nextSequenceStep() instance Advances according to loop policy. getSequenceState() state object Returns current playback state. Sequence state Field Type Description configured boolean Whether steps exist. running boolean Whether sequence time advances. completed boolean Whether a non-looping sequence reached its final boundary. index number Active step index or -1. length number Step count. loop boolean Active loop policy. elapsed number Seconds elapsed in the current phase. waiting boolean Whether the active step delay is pending. loading boolean Whether the active step is waiting for an image decode. Duration remains at zero. morphing boolean Whether an outgoing snapshot is currently fading. morphProgress number Normalized morph progress from 0 through 1. Events Subscribe with on(event, listener). The method returns an unsubscribe function. Remove a known listener with off(event, listener).
app.js
const unsubscribe = animation.on('rendererFallback', (detail, instance) => { console.log(detail.reason, detail.backend, instance); }); unsubscribe(); Keep the returned unsubscribe function when a listener belongs to a component lifecycle. off(event, listener) is useful when the same stable listener reference is already available.
Event Trigger ready Construction and initial sizing complete. resize Target grid dimensions change. frame A frame is rendered. rendererChange Requested or resolved renderer changes. rendererFallback WebGL context loss switches presentation to Canvas 2D. imageFramesReady Exact GIF capture completes; detail includes frameCount and total duration in seconds. meshReady, meshClear Retained geometry is installed or released. modelLoadStart, modelProgress Model loading starts or reports transferred bytes. modelReady, modelError, modelClear Model normalization succeeds, fails, or is cleared. sequenceStart, sequenceResume Sequence playback starts or resumes. sequencePause, sequenceStop Playback pauses or stops. sequenceLoop, sequenceComplete Sequence loops or finishes. sequenceInterrupt Manual mode selection interrupts playback. sequenceStepStart A delayed or immediate step starts. sequenceStepComplete A step reaches its duration. sequenceStepInterrupt Seek, stop, reconfiguration, or manual input interrupts a step. sequenceStepError A step image fails to decode; detail contains error and playback pauses. sequenceMorphStart, sequenceMorphComplete A snapshot morph begins or finishes. Callback types Callback Signature Description Ready (animation) => void Constructor readiness callback. Image error (error) => void Image decode or load failure callback. Event listener (detail, animation) => void General event subscription. Sequence callback (detail, animation) => void Step or sequence lifecycle callback. Custom cell (api) => cell | null Returns a glyph cell for one grid coordinate. TypeScript surface The bundled declarations export asciiamMode, asciiamEvent, asciiamOptions, sequence step/options/state types, event detail, and the default asciiam class. Import types alongside the runtime without a separate package.
import asciiam, { type asciiamOptions, type asciiamSequenceStep } from '@staticcanvas/asciiam'; const options: asciiamOptions = { renderer: 'auto', quality: 'balanced' }; const steps: asciiamSequenceStep[] = [ { mode: 'ripple', duration: 5 }, { mode: 'fadeOut', duration: 1.2 } ]; const animation = new asciiam('#target', options).setSequence(steps, { loop: true, autoplay: true });
title: API reference

description: Sample local or remote images into ASCII and restrict animation to an inclusive RGB range.
text: Image loading establishes a sampled glyph source. Static images are resampled after grid or image-option changes. Animated GIFs capture each composited frame as an ASCII grid when WebCodecs ImageDecoder is available. Brightness selects glyph density. Optional sampled RGB values color each glyph. The global mode then animates that source, so the same mode inventory applies to procedural and image-backed output. Load an image app.js await animation.setImage('/images/subject.webp'); animation.setMode('ripple'); animation.setOption('colorFromImage', true); Uploaded files can be passed through an object URL. Revoke the URL after setImage() resolves. URL paths ending in .gif are detected automatically. Object URLs do not retain a filename, so pass { animated: true } when loading an uploaded GIF. setImage() waits while each decoded frame is converted to the current ASCII grid, preserves the GIF’s individual frame delays, and emits imageFramesReady with frameCount and total duration. The decoded bitmap for each frame is closed immediately; playback retains ASCII data, not full-resolution frames. If ImageDecoder or fetch access is unavailable, asciiam falls back to sampling the browser-animated . imageFrameRate limits only that compatibility path and does not cap renderer FPS. Changing image sampling options or target dimensions re-captures the ASCII frames after a short debounce. app.js await animation.setImage(objectUrl, { animated: file.type === 'image/gif' }); animation.setOption('imageFrameRate', 12); Animate a colour range app.js animation.setOption('imageAnimationRange', { min: '#7a0000', max: '#ff8a70' }); animation.setMode('ripple'); Every built-in mode can operate while an image source is loaded. Dense modes animate the sampled glyph cells directly. Sparse modes such as matrix, snow, fire, starfield, and orbit retain their particle geometry and are clipped to sampled image cells. Transparent SVG silhouettes often use black fills. Normal luminance mapping sends black to the first density glyph, which is commonly a space. The default imageLuminance: 'auto' detects dark opaque artwork surrounded by transparency and inverts its density mapping. Set normal or invert when explicit control is required. This affects glyph density only; it does not rotate or transform the source SVG. Image fitting compares the source aspect ratio with the rendered glyph area, including the measured glyph width and line height. imageScale and imageFov change the centered source window. imageScaleX and imageScaleY then change the centered sampled output width and height. This distinction preserves the source ratio by default while allowing intentional horizontal or vertical distortion. ASCII text sources JavaScript FIGlet implementations can convert text into multiline ASCII banners before rendering. The figlet package provides browser and ESM builds and implements the FIGfont format. Keep it as an application-level optional adapter so asciiam retains zero runtime dependencies: generate the banner, rasterize it to a canvas or SVG data URL, then pass that result to setImage() and select any global mode. The engine creates a byte mask during image sampling. Per-frame image animation checks the mask rather than repeating RGB range comparisons. Cells outside the range remain static. Mask modes Value Behavior waveSweep Moves a horizontal intensity band through selected cells. radialRipple Propagates from the configured spatial origin. scanlinePass Moves a narrow scanline over selected cells. thermalNoise Applies time-varying seeded noise. halftonePulse Pulses a spatial halftone pattern. fullStatic Displays sampled glyphs without mask animation. API reference Property or method Type Default Effect setImage(source, options?) URL string and optional { animated } — Decodes an image and captures all GIF frames where supported. fit cover | contain cover Crops or letterboxes the source. imageScale number 1 Applies centered source zoom. imageScaleX number 1 Scales sampled output width around the centre. imageScaleY number 1 Scales sampled output height around the centre. imageFov number 1 Controls the sampled field of view. imageLuminance auto | normal | invert auto Controls silhouette-aware brightness mapping. imageChars string active character set Maps brightness to glyphs. colorFromImage boolean false Uses sampled RGB values. animateImageMask boolean true Enables legacy mode: 'image' mask animation; global modes animate image sources independently. imageAnimationRange { min, max } or null null Restricts animation to an inclusive RGB box. animateImageFrames boolean true Plays captured or fallback-sampled GIF frames. imageFrameRate number 12 Caps fallback GIF sampling from 1 through 60 fps.
title: Images and colour-range animation

description: Render typed-array meshes, procedural primitives, and dependency-free glTF 2.0 or GLB v2 files as ASCII.
text:
The mesh mode projects geometry into a cell-resolution depth and luminance buffer. The normal asciiam glyph pipeline then presents those cells through WebGL2 or Canvas 2D. It is a bounded ASCII source, not a general scene engine: materials, textures, animation clips, skins, cameras, and lights from glTF are not rendered.
Procedural geometry const animation = new asciiam('#target', { mode: 'mesh', meshPrimitive: 'torus', meshStyle: 'wireframe', meshAutoRotate: true }); animation.start(); cube, plane, icosphere, and torus are generated at construction time without bundled model assets. For explicit control, call asciiam.createMeshPrimitive(name, options) and pass the result to setMesh().
Application geometry animation.setMesh({ positions: new Float32Array([ 0, 1, 0, -1, -1, 0, 1, -1, 0 ]), indices: new Uint16Array([0, 1, 2]), primitive: 'triangles' }); animation.setMode('mesh'); Positions are XYZ triples. Optional normals must be a matching Float32Array; optional colours contain one RGBA Float32 tuple per vertex. Indices may be unsigned 8-, 16-, or 32-bit arrays. Invalid lengths, non-finite positions, out-of-range indices, incomplete primitives, and configured complexity-limit violations are rejected before rendering.
glTF and GLB await animation.setModel('/models/product.glb', { onProgress({ loaded, total }) { console.log(total ? loaded / total : loaded); } }); animation.setMode('mesh'); setModel() accepts a URL, Blob, ArrayBuffer, typed-array view, or parsed glTF object. It supports glTF 2.0 JSON, GLB v2, data URIs, relative external buffers, interleaved accessors, sparse accessors, node hierarchies and transforms, vertex normals and colours, scene selection, and all core point/line/triangle primitive modes. A new load cancels the previous load. clearModel() cancels pending work and releases the retained geometry.
Required extensions are rejected with their names before scene mesh allocation. In particular, Draco and Meshopt decoders are not bundled, downloaded, or injectable. This keeps model behavior deterministic and the runtime dependency-free.
Controls and events API Default Purpose meshStyle wireframe points, wireframe, or solid cell rasterization. meshProjection perspective Perspective or orthographic projection. meshCamera internal camera Position, target, up vector, field of view, clipping planes, and orthographic scale. meshTransform identity Position, Euler rotation in radians, and scale. meshLight one directional light Direction, ambient contribution, and intensity. meshAutoRotate true Applies meshRotationSpeed against elapsed time. meshMaxVertices 100000 Rejects larger normalized geometry. meshMaxPrimitives 100000 Rejects larger point, line, or triangle counts. Model loading emits modelLoadStart, modelProgress, modelReady, modelError, and modelClear. Geometry changes emit meshReady and meshClear.
Asset and delivery policy Poly Haven publishes CC0 models. Khronos glTF Sample Assets provides format examples, but each model’s license must be checked individually. glTF/GLB is the supported import format; no third-party model is bundled with the package. See Attributions before adding a demonstration asset.
Run npm run benchmark:mesh after changing projection or rasterization code. The development reference scene contains 960 vertices and 1,920 triangles at a 60×45 cell grid; the enforced desktop gate is 4 ms median and 8 ms p95.
title: 3D meshes and models

description: Release history and behavior changes for asciiam.
text:
0.10.0 Current documented baseline. This release establishes the public renderer, animation, sequencing, image-sampling, and web-utility contracts reflected in the API reference.
Runtime WebGL2 renderer with instanced glyph batching, shader gradients, trail and backdrop blending, and Canvas 2D fallback. Runtime renderer selection through auto, webgl2, and canvas2d. Ordered animation sequences with delays, durations, independent per-step mode repeat, whole-sequence looping, interruption, callbacks, and lifecycle events. Replaying a completed sequence restarts from step zero. Sequence nodes can retain, clear, or asynchronously replace image sources. Node timing waits for decoding; failures pause playback and emit sequenceStepError. Dense, spatial, reveal, sparse-particle, image, and custom animation modes. Added irisIn, irisOut, dissolveIn, dissolveOut, lumaFold, riftLace, and echoBloom, with the global mode inventory available to image-backed output. Added hoverZone and clickZone for pointer-local and triggered interaction fields, with programmatic setCursor() and triggerInteraction() control. Expanded spatial alignment to a nine-position grid for every mode with a meaningful configurable origin. Added compact technical, geometric, circuit, wave, terminal, and minimal character sets while retaining asciiExtended as the documented default. Backdrops accept explicit behind or over placement. Exact opacity 1 in the over layer fully covers the glyph animation. Image-to-ASCII sampling with mask modes, inclusive RGB animation ranges, and independent centered horizontal and vertical output scaling. Image fitting now uses rendered glyph-cell dimensions instead of treating ASCII cells as square, preserving source proportions. Animated GIF sources capture every composited frame into an ASCII grid through WebCodecs ImageDecoder, preserve per-frame timing, and release decoded bitmaps immediately. Browser-timed sampling remains the fallback; imageFrameRate controls only that compatibility path. imageLuminance adds auto, normal, and invert mappings. Auto mode detects dark artwork on transparency so common black silhouette SVGs map to visible glyphs. Image sampling reuses its readback canvas and retains glyph atlases while animated frames change. Shared frame scheduling, visibility pausing, quality tiers, glyph atlases, and static-wave caching. Web utility Interactive web utility with preset editing, undo and redo, generated code, renderer selection, local image upload, animated-image controls, independent image-axis controls, and luminance mapping. Sequence steps expose a mode-repeat switch enabled by default for utility previews; exported configuration retains the explicit value. Replaced the vertical sequence stack with an ordered node flow and per-node image-source controls. Split web-utility behavior into a module entry point plus focused code-formatting and sequence-data modules; documentation scripts remain separated by site-wide and page-specific responsibility. Kept Reset in the primary dock and aligned Documentation, About, and FPS as direct stage actions. Character-set selection includes the expanded built-in inventory; interaction modes expose radius and duration controls; spatial alignment exposes all nine anchors. Versioned runtime loading and revalidated local library caching prevent new controls from executing against an older renderer bundle. Image-library cards use generated static 320×180 WebP previews, first-frame GIF thumbnails, low-priority lazy decoding, and off-screen content containment. Opening the Image popover no longer decodes every original media asset. Documentation Hugo documentation source and visibility-bounded live preset gallery. Full constructor, option, method, renderer, sequence, event, and callback reference. Web-utility workflow, preset gallery, version policy, GIF/SVG behavior, and integration guides. Default and included character sets are documented in a focused guide and the repository README. Added a single-instance live usage workbench with minimum-to-complete JSON-safe examples, reset/copy controls, and web-utility configuration transfer. Added page descriptions, dates, tags, keywords, modified-time metadata, and GitLab/GitHub edit links across the documentation set. Added / alongside Ctrl+K and Command+K for current-page search focus. Hardened site search with combobox semantics, deduplicated index loading, stale-query suppression, malformed-field tolerance, and deploy-path-safe result links. Expanded search metadata and vocabulary aliases, added safe literal-word highlighting, and visually selected matching tag chips. Made the documentation root a chrome-free splash with an asciiam-rendered background; inner documentation pages retain navigation and search. Corrected the splash height to 100svh on desktop and mobile so its canvas owns the complete initial viewport and documentation content begins below the fold. Added maintained Lucide, SVG Repo, PAT, media-provider, registry, and delivery-service attribution references. Compatibility Canonical .mjs ESM and .cjs CommonJS package entries are provided alongside the readable/minified browser ESM and UMD bundles. Canvas 2D and requestAnimationFrame are required. WebGL2, IntersectionObserver, and ResizeObserver are feature-detected. Upgrade notes This is the first documented API baseline; there are no earlier documented migrations. Prefer renderer: 'auto' when the application should use WebGL2 where available and retain Canvas 2D fallback. Call destroy() when removing an instance so observers, listeners, renderer resources, and scheduler membership are released. Pass { animated: true } to setImage() for uploaded GIF object URLs because blob URLs do not retain the original filename or MIME type. Use imageLuminance: 'normal' when automatic silhouette detection is not appropriate for a transparent source.
title: Changelog

description: Configure, validate, export, and persist asciiam settings in the browser utility.
text:
The web utility is an authoring surface for asciiam option objects; detailed runtime behavior remains defined by the package API.
Configure a composition Start with a preset or animation mode, then adjust renderer, quality, character density, spatial origin, motion, color, backdrop, and image controls. Undo and Redo operate on the current browser session. Reset restores utility defaults without deleting named presets.
The Character set control includes the documented asciiExtended default, ordered density ramps, symbolic palettes, and a custom string editor. Hover Zone and Click Zone expose radius and click-duration controls in Motion. Align provides nine spatial anchors.
The dock keeps Preset, Sequence, Mode, Motion, Color, Reset, Image, and Code directly available. Advanced contains lower-frequency quality, character-set, alignment, backdrop, theme, and history controls. Reset intentionally remains outside Advanced. Documentation, About, and the FPS switch form one level action row on the stage.
The sequence editor is a horizontally ordered node flow. Each node edits its animation, image-source action, duration, stagger, repeat policy, transition, and JSON option overrides. Nodes can retain or clear the current image, or load an included image; reordering changes playback order immediately.
Preview presentation types Background, Hero card, and Splash page are presentation previews rather than HTML overlays generated by asciiam. Each preview gives the renderer a bounded target and places ordinary interface content beside or above it.
Hero and Splash can use an uploaded or included image as the ASCII source. The image is sampled into glyph density and optional sampled color; the original bitmap is not placed over the preview. Use cover or contain, image scale, field of view, the global animation mode, and an optional inclusive RGB animation range to control the result.
Preview Purpose Runtime implication Background Evaluate a full-stage ASCII surface behind application content. One target sized to the stage. Hero card Evaluate ASCII image or procedural media inside a bounded content card. One renderer attached to the card media region. Splash page Evaluate a larger introductory composition and transition sequence. One renderer attached to the splash media region. Validate performance Choose auto to request WebGL2 first and retain Canvas 2D fallback. Enable the FPS panel to inspect the resolved backend, frame rate, cell count, and quality tier. Test the composition at the actual target size because density, DPR, glyph count, and image sampling work change with dimensions.
For grids and galleries, construct only visible previews and destroy instances that leave the working set. All running instances share a frame scheduler, but each WebGL2 context and glyph buffer still consumes browser resources.
Export and integrate Open Code to generate a constructor option object from the current controls. Install the package or select a browser bundle, create an instance after its target has measurable dimensions, then call start().
app.js
import asciiam from '@staticcanvas/asciiam'; const animation = new asciiam('#hero-media', { ...asciiam.presets.heroWave, renderer: 'auto' }); animation.start(); Call destroy() when removing the target. This releases observers, subscriptions, presentation resources, and an owned canvas.
The Usage examples workbench provides a second authoring path. Its View in web utility action sends the current JSON-safe options through a base64url-encoded config query value. The utility applies that configuration after defaults and locally restored settings, then exposes it as a custom composition. Invalid or non-object values are ignored.
Persistence and local data Data Persistence Utility options Stored in versioned browser local storage. Named presets Stored locally in the current browser. Undo and redo history Retained for the current page session. Uploaded images Browser-local object URLs; not restored on the next visit. Included image manifest Generated from public/assets/images by npm run prepare:bg. Generated code Derived from current state and not stored separately. Documentation routes Use Getting started for package and browser initialization. Use Renderers and performance for backend and quality behavior. Use Images and colour-range animation for sampled media. Use Animation sequences for staggered and interruptible flows. Use Usage examples for editable minimum-to-complete configurations. Use the API reference for option and method contracts. API reference Utility control Runtime option or API Default behavior Renderer renderer, setRenderer() auto; WebGL2 first, Canvas 2D fallback. Quality quality, maxDPR, targetFPS Uses the selected quality tier. Mode mode, setMode() Selects the active cell algorithm. Motion and Align speed, edgeFade, trail, pulse, align Updates animation and spatial state. Color and Backdrop color, gradient, backdrop Configures glyph and independent backdrop presentation. Image setImage(), image options Samples a local or remote image into the glyph grid. Sequence setSequence(), sequence methods Configures ordered animation steps. Code constructor options Serializes the current supported configuration. config URL value JSON-safe constructor options Imports a documentation example without depending on npm or a CDN. Backdrop placement is explicit. behind draws before glyphs. over composites after glyphs, so opacity 1 fully covers the animation. The range and exact numeric input both accept the inclusive interval from 0 through 1.
The Image popover exposes centered uniform, horizontal, and vertical scaling; field of view; silhouette-aware luminance mapping; animated-image playback and sample rate; sampled color; and an optional RGB animation range. The global Mode popover remains the animation selector after an image is loaded.
npm run prepare:bg generates static 320×180 WebP menu previews when ImageMagick is available. GIF previews use the first frame and image orientation is normalized during generation. Opening the Image popover therefore decodes bounded static previews, not full-resolution sources or animated GIF streams. An original asset is loaded only after its card is selected.

description: Source, license, and service references for icons, demonstration media, future mesh research, registries, and delivery infrastructure.
text:
This page identifies third-party material and external services referenced by the repository; it does not change the MIT license applied to asciiam source code.
Embedded icon paths The documentation navigation embeds a local subset of Lucide SVG paths. Lucide is distributed under the ISC License, and some Lucide designs derive from Feather under the MIT License. The redistributed notices are preserved in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
Icons are embedded locally so documentation navigation does not depend on a client-side icon package or third-party request.
Bundled SVG demonstration asset public/assets/images/bird-silhouette.svg is the Bird Shape vector from SVG Repo. SVG Repo identifies that asset as CC0. The file remains a demonstration input for silhouette-aware image-to-ASCII conversion.
Map reference public/assets/images/earth-landmask-256-slow.gif uses a globe land-mask source associated with PAT, the free, open-source portable atlas. PAT states that its maps and generating scripts are public domain.
Demonstration photographs The image library contains development and rendering-test media sourced from Pexels, Pixabay, and local repository contributions. Provider and creator identifiers are retained in filenames where available. Provider references are not blanket license claims: verify an individual source record before redistributing an asset outside this repository.
3D model sources and format references asciiam bundles no third-party 3D models. Its dependency-free glTF/GLB loader uses the following format and candidate asset sources:
Poly Haven models are published under Poly Haven’s CC0 asset license. Record the exact model source and metadata before including one in a demonstration or test fixture. Khronos glTF Sample Assets provide format test cases and example models. Each model carries its own license and credit record; check the selected model directory before use or redistribution. The glTF 2.0 specification defines the core glTF/GLB input boundary. Base-format parsing ships in the main package without external dependencies. Assets requiring Draco, Meshopt, or another compression extension will be rejected. Codec evaluation is deferred research and no decoder or decoder hook is planned for the released runtime. These references do not grant a blanket license for assets obtained elsewhere.
External project services GitLab and GitHub host source mirrors and page editing. npm and JSR are package registries. jsDelivr and unpkg provide package CDN delivery after publication. Shields.io supplies README badges. These services are not runtime dependencies of the asciiam library.
